title: Atlas — From source to structure
direction: Warm editorial product film. Atlas ink, white, warm neutrals and terracotta. Deliberate camera moves, crisp ledgers, tracing lines and generous type.
message: Move from physical metadata to reviewed models, mappings and SQL in one governed workspace.
audio: Original locally synthesized instrumental bed; no voiceover. The complete story is readable with sound off.
assets: Existing Atlas logo; code-built product illustrations using fictional metadata. No live data or external services.
accuracy: Mark product illustrations as demo data.
Model diagrams illustrate authored outputs; they do not imply an interactive graph editor.
Generated SQL is a reviewable artifact, not an executed or deployed pipeline.
Candidate validation, explicit Apply and model revision are separate steps.
Do not invent a launch date, public URL, performance claim or customer claim.

scenes.headline: From source to structure.
scenes.visual: Atlas identity and a sweeping product-window reveal; physical objects begin aligning into a model.

scenes.headline: Know your starting point.
scenes.support: Explore metadata. Profile attributes. Enrich context.
scenes.visual: Recreated metadata ledger, selected object, then a close view of an attribute profile with measured results.

scenes.headline: Give your data structure.
scenes.visual: Illustrated conceptual-to-logical-to-dimensional progression; relationship lines build with each entity.

scenes.headline: Carry the logic through.
scenes.support: From source mappings to reviewable SQL.
scenes.visual: A mapping ledger expands into a light SQL editor; matched source identifiers maintain a visual trace into the generated SELECT artifact.

scenes.headline: Every change. Yours to review.
scenes.visual: A draft moves through candidate validation and review. Explicit Apply advances revision 12 to 13 and shows its receipt. No query execution is implied.

scenes.headline: Build with context.
scenes.visual: The scene resolves to the real Atlas mark and wordmark, a terracotta rule, and a clear final invitation.

timing: 1260 scene frames minus 60 overlap frames = 1200 frames / 30 fps = 40 seconds.
